history.heading: The Grimaldis
paragraphs: Monaco, a tiny city-state on the French Riviera, was founded as a Genoese colony in 1215. In 1297 François Grimaldi, disguised as a monk, seized the fortress on the Rock; the Grimaldi family has ruled Monaco, with brief interruptions, ever since, making it one of the oldest ruling dynasties in Europe.

Monaco was under Spanish and then French protection. It lost the towns of Menton and Roquebrune, about 95 percent of its territory, in 1848 and formally ceded them to France in 1861 in exchange for recognition of its independence.

history.heading: Casino and glamour
paragraphs: To compensate for lost revenues, Prince Charles III opened a casino at Monte Carlo in the 1860s, which, with the arrival of the railway, made Monaco a glamorous resort. Prince Rainier III, who reigned from 1949 to 2005, married American actress Grace Kelly in 1956 and diversified the economy. His son Albert II has reigned since 2005.

culture.heading: Riviera life
paragraphs: French is the official language, and Monégasque, a Ligurian dialect, is taught in schools. Monégasque citizens are a minority of residents; most are foreigners, many attracted by the tax regime. Catholicism is the state religion.

Monaco hosts the Monaco Grand Prix, one of the most famous Formula One races, the Monte-Carlo Rally and the Monte-Carlo Masters tennis tournament. The Oceanographic Museum, once directed by Jacques Cousteau, is famous. AS Monaco plays in the French football league.

politics.heading: Constitutional monarchy
paragraphs: Monaco is a constitutional monarchy in which the Sovereign Prince holds significant executive power. The government is led by a minister of state, and the National Council is an elected parliament. France is responsible for Monaco's defence. Monaco is not in the EU but uses the euro and is linked to the EU customs union.

economy.heading: Wealth and tourism
paragraphs: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world and the most densely populated. There is no personal income tax for residents (except French citizens), attracting wealthy residents. The economy relies on tourism, banking and wealth management, real estate, which is among the most expensive in the world, and the casino. Land has been reclaimed from the sea to expand the territory.
